column12: Judgement: this is a published list price, which the book puts ahead of the CMS convention, but it belongs to the comparator and not to velzatinib. Qinlock is the closest marketed KIT inhibitor in GIST. Cross-check on the CMS basis: Qinlock's Medicare Part D 2025 (Q1-Q4) spend was $126,600,395.66 over 536 beneficiaries, $236,194.77 each at 5.25 fills a beneficiary (CMS Part D quarterly dataset 4ff7c618-4e40-483a-b390-c8a58c94fa15). A treated patient in Medicare filled 44% of a year, so this full-year WAC bills each treated patient more than the average Qinlock patient pays in a calendar year; that is the main case for a lower price. Ayvakit, the other branded GIST KIT inhibitor, ran $323,698.51 a 2025 beneficiary, but most of its use is systemic mastocytosis. The generic comparators (sunitinib, imatinib) cost a small fraction of this. A second-line drug may also launch below a fourth-line one. In GBP because the engine models a company in its reporting currency and converts to dollars only at the end: $567,210.00 at GBP/USD 1.327632 (ECB via fetchers/fx_ecb.py, 2026-09-23, the fx_rates row the other GSK seeds use) is GBP 427,234.24

column11: Three sourced parts. (1) 5,234 of 31,019 staged cases (16.87%) were distant at diagnosis (Patel & Benipal, Cureus 2019;11(2):e4120, PMID 31037234, Table 1). (2) Estimated 15-year recurrence-free survival after surgery without adjuvant therapy was 59.9%, so 40.1% recur (Joensuu H et al., Lancet Oncol 2012;13:265-74, doi:10.1016/S1470-2045(11)70299-6, PMID 22153892, 2,560 patients pooled). 0.1687 + 0.8313 x 0.401 = 0.5021 of each year's diagnoses reach advanced disease. (3) The label reach: StrateGIST 3 (NCT07218926; ASCO 2026 TPS11588) excludes GIST that is wild-type for both KIT and PDGFRA and GIST with an activating PDGFRA exon 18 mutation. In advanced GIST (MetaGIST) KIT mutations are found in 82.8% and PDGFRA in 2.1% (Emile JF et al., Med Oncol 2012;29(3):1765-72, doi:10.1007/s12032-011-0074-y, PMID 21953054). 0.5021 x 0.828 = 0.4157
column12: Judgement: assumes every KIT-mutant patient reaching advanced disease eventually fails imatinib and is fit for a second line, and that the label follows the trial's exclusions. The case for lower: adjuvant imatinib now delays or prevents some recurrences, some patients stay on first-line imatinib for years, and some die or decline before second line. The case for higher: the incidence rate is out of date and rising, and non-exon-18 PDGFRA mutants (a share of the 2.1%) are eligible but left out here

column11: Two parts. (1) Sunitinib's measured second-line share: Hsu JT et al., Oncotarget 2017;8(41):71128-37, doi:10.18632/oncotarget.16795, PMID 29050348 (Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database, July 2004 to December 2010): of 521 advanced GIST patients failing first-line imatinib 400 mg and treated with dose escalation or sunitinib, 125 escalated then switched to sunitinib and 150 switched directly, so 275 (52.78%) received sunitinib after imatinib. (2) An order-of-entry cut, because velzatinib will not be the first branded drug to beat sunitinib in second line: Cogent's bezuclastinib plus sunitinib beat sunitinib in the PEAK Phase 3 (median PFS 16.5 against 9.2 months, HR 0.50, Cogent 8-K 10 November 2025) and its NDA was accepted with priority review and a PDUFA date of 2026-11-30 (Cogent release, 28 May 2026), more than three years before velzatinib's 2030 start. Urban et al., Management Science 1986, put a second entrant's share at 2^-0.49 = 0.712 of the pioneer's, so the second of two takes 0.712 / 1.712 = 41.59% of the class. 0.5278 x 0.4159 = 0.2195
column12: JUDGEMENT on the multiple, the formula the zigakibart seed cross-checks with. The case for higher: velzatinib is a single agent where the pioneer is a two-drug combination carrying sunitinib's toxicity, its second-line cohort showed a 13.7-month median PFS, and a PFS win could also displace imatinib dose escalation, which the 52.8% leaves out. The case for lower: StrateGIST 3 compares against sunitinib alone, not the combination that will be standard by readout, so velzatinib may launch without a head-to-head answer to it; Hsu's denominator excludes patients who received neither option, so the share overstates capture of this pool; the setting is Taiwan, not the US. Bezuclastinib is not in the book, so pool_crowding cannot see it and the cut has to sit here.
